workflows.title: Inspect a project
workflows.summary: Build a compact, evidence-based picture of the repository before changing it.

steps.purpose: Find the repository root and read applicable project/agent instructions.
Identify language, framework, package manager, entry points, and documented scripts from manifests and README files.
Check the current Git branch and worktree without modifying it.
Summarize the relevant architecture, current changes, and likely files to inspect next.

workflows.title: Review Git changes
workflows.summary: Inspect staged, unstaged, and untracked changes without changing the worktree.

steps.purpose: Show branch and working-tree state.
Summarize unstaged changes.
Check unstaged diff whitespace errors.
Inspect staged and unstaged diffs separately, then review untracked filenames. Do not assume untracked files are safe to add.
Report findings by severity and cite affected paths/lines where possible.

workflows.title: Run relevant tests
workflows.summary: Discover the project's test command and run the smallest useful test set first.

steps.purpose: Inspect project instructions, manifests, lockfiles, and documented test scripts.
Select targeted tests relevant to the changed behavior; do not guess the package manager or test runner.
Run the selected test command, capture its exit status, and report exact scope.
Run broader tests only when proportionate; distinguish not-run from passed.

workflows.title: Run quality checks
workflows.summary: Find and run project-defined lint, type, format, and build checks that apply to the change.

steps.purpose: Discover available lint, type-check, formatter, and build scripts in project configuration.
Choose checks relevant to the edited files and invoke them separately when their failure causes differ.
Report pass/fail/skip for each check; do not silently install missing tooling.

workflows.title: Prepare a focused commit
workflows.summary: Review and propose a focused commit; stage and commit only within the user's authorized scope.

steps.purpose: Inspect all tracked and untracked changes before selecting files.
Review diffs and group related files. Exclude unrelated, generated, local, and secret-bearing files.
Present the exact proposed file list and commit message before staging if the scope is not already explicit.
Stage only reviewed paths, inspect the staged diff, and commit only when the user's request authorizes the commit.
Pushing is a separate external action; never infer permission to push from permission to commit.

workflows.title: Prepare a release checklist
workflows.summary: Assess release readiness without tagging, publishing, pushing, or deploying.

steps.purpose: Inspect branch/worktree state, versioning files, changelog, release docs, and CI status.
Discover the repository's documented build and release validation steps.
Run appropriate local checks and produce a release checklist with blockers.
Tagging, pushing, publishing, and deploying require separate explicit authorization for the exact target.

workflows.title: Inspect dependencies
workflows.summary: Identify package manager and dependency risks without automatically changing versions.

steps.purpose: Identify package manager and lockfile; inspect direct dependency declarations.
Check project policy and available audit/report commands before running them.
Dependency updates, removals, and installs change the environment or lockfile; propose them before applying.
Separate confirmed findings, advisories, and unknowns in the report.

workflows.title: Cross-platform command
workflows.summary: Select and validate a readable command for the detected operating system and shell.

steps.purpose: Detect OS, shell, working directory, and available tools.
Prefer native tools or project scripts before shell commands.
Review side effects and obtain required approval before mutation or external actions.
Execute through the host agent and verify the result.

workflows.title: Refactor long command
workflows.summary: Explain a long shell command and propose a clearer equivalent without silently changing semantics.

steps.purpose: Parse logical stages, operators, quoting, redirection, and shell assumptions.
Compare native tools, API, project scripts, and structured argv.
Review proposed behavior and approval boundaries before execution.
Verify equivalence and report limitations.

workflows.title: Agent tool selection
workflows.summary: Choose between agent-native tools, project scripts, CLI, API, and SDK.

steps.purpose: Discover available native tools and project automation.
Compare reliability, permissions, portability, and output quality.
Choose the smallest reliable workflow and verify its result.
